class.name: RealitySceneTree
class.brief_description: Synchronizes Godot scenes and manages independent visionOS volumes.
class.description: Volume ID 0 identifies the main volumetric scene. Additional IDs increase monotonically and are never reused during this scene tree's lifetime. These IDs are unrelated to [DisplayServer] window IDs. Each additional volume owns a separate scene, [SubViewport], [World3D], camera and input scope. Native 2D windows continue to use [Window]. [method close_volume_window] keeps the scene and ID; [method destroy_volume_window] releases an additional volume after its native host and rendering work have ended. Methods returning [enum Error] return [constant OK] when accepted, not when presentation has finished. Observe [signal volume_window_state_changed] and [signal volume_window_operation_failed]. Native volume creation requires visionOS and volumetric presentation. System and user control determine placement; this API does not set world positions.

method.name: open_volume_window
method.description: Instantiates a packed scene and requests a new volume. Returns its ID, or -1 for an unavailable presentation, invalid options or scene load failure. A later native activation failure leaves the allocated volume [constant CLOSED] and retryable. Options are copied before the scene enters the tree.

method.name: reopen_volume_window
method.description: Requests presentation of the existing scene. Repeated opens coalesce. An open during closing runs after closure completes. Unknown IDs return [constant ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST].

method.name: close_volume_window
method.description: Requests closure, invalidates poses and cancels only this volume's haptics. Scene, ID and trackers are retained. A system close has the same result. Unknown IDs return [constant ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST].

method.name: destroy_volume_window
method.description: Stops input and destroys an additional volume asynchronously. Removes its trackers and haptic requests. ID 0 returns [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE]. Repeated destruction requests coalesce. Unknown IDs return [constant ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST].

method.name: get_volume_window_ids
method.description: Returns all retained IDs in ascending order, including closed and destroying volumes.

method.name: has_volume_window
method.description: Returns whether the ID is retained. Remains true until destruction finishes.

method.name: get_volume_window_state
method.description: Returns the current lifecycle state, or [constant INVALID] for an unknown ID.

method.name: get_volume_window_root
method.description: Returns the scene root, or null for an invalid ID or a scene that has exited.

method.name: get_volume_window_viewport
method.description: Returns the volume viewport, or null for an invalid ID. The main volume uses the root [Window].

method.name: get_volume_window_id
method.description: Returns the owning volume ID. Returns -1 for null, detached nodes, or nodes inside ordinary 2D windows.

method.name: get_volume_window_title
method.description: Returns the stored title, or an empty string for an unknown ID.

method.name: set_volume_window_title
method.description: Updates the native scene title and title ornament. Returns [constant ERR_BUSY] during destruction.

method.name: get_volume_window_options
method.description: Returns a copy of the applied preferences, or null for an invalid ID. Mutating this copy has no effect until passed to the setter.

method.name: set_volume_window_options
method.description: Copies and applies preferences. Null resets preferences. Initial size is used on the next open; limits, resizing and baseplate visibility update the existing host. Invalid minimum/maximum bounds return [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER].

method.name: get_volume_window_size
method.description: Returns the last system-reported physical extent in meters, independent of the Godot camera/world scale. Zero means no measurement yet or an invalid ID. This is not the requested size.

signal.name: volume_window_state_changed
signal.description: Emitted when a retained volume changes state.

signal.name: volume_window_operation_failed
signal.description: Emitted for a native open, close or configuration failure, or scene load failure (ID -1). A configuration failure does not close the host.

signal.name: volume_window_size_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the physical extent changes. Size is measured in meters.

signal.name: volume_window_destroyed
signal.description: Emitted after the host, scene loader and trackers are detached and the viewport has been deleted. The ID is no longer valid.

constants.constant: Retained scene without an open host.
